Follow-up to LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6 (related-to:LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6).

The proxy now supports persisted fast/cheap operating modes switched manually via API/UI. Add an automatic time-based scheduler so the mode follows the clock:

- cheap mode is active from 00:01 until 10:00 (local server time)
- fast mode is active from 10:00 until 00:01 (i.e. 10:00 through midnight, plus 00:00-00:01)

The timer ENFORCES the schedule regardless of the currently active setting: a manual API/UI switch away from the scheduled mode is reverted by the next scheduler check. Mode changes triggered by the timer use the same set_mode() path as manual switches (persist proxy/.mode + background restart via start-proxy.sh --restart).

Design: reuse the existing slot_schedule-style config pattern with a new 'mode_schedule' section (entries time->mode, most-recent-entry-before-now with circular wrap so 10:00->fast also covers 00:00-00:01), plus a background loop in the proxy (similar to the slot scheduler) that checks periodically (and immediately at startup, so a restart at 10:05 applies the scheduled mode without waiting). Same section in config.yaml / config-fast.yaml / config-cheap.yaml; disabled via enabled: false; absent section falls back to the built-in schedule.

Acceptance criteria:
- expected_mode_for_time() returns cheap for 00:01..<10:00 and fast for 10:00..<00:01 (wrap: 00:00-00:00:59 is fast), in local server time
- A background loop in the proxy applies the scheduled mode when the persisted mode diverges (reverting manual overrides), skips when a restart is pending, and checks immediately at startup
- mode_schedule config section parses (enabled flag + entries), invalid entries are ignored with a warning, section absent -> built-in default schedule
- mode changes from the timer persist proxy/.mode and trigger the same background restart as manual switches
- Full project test suite passes; docs (proxy/README.md) updated
data.title: Time-based automatic mode switching (cheap 00:01-10:00, fast 10:00-00:01)

data.description:
The proxy-usage-analysis skill's fast/cheap bucketing is wrong for windows spanning a mode transition.

## Problem

The analysis script (analyze_proxy_usage.py) derives the fast/cheap bucket split from the slot_schedule of the config profile for the mode active AT ANALYSIS TIME (config-fast.yaml / config-cheap.yaml per proxy/.mode). It never reconstructs the mode that was actually active DURING the analyzed window.

Observed failure (2026-08-12 window 01:00-11:47):
- The proxy ran CHEAP mode 01:00-10:00 (log evidence: 'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode cheap' at 01:00:20; status lines show total_slots=2 + contention_queue_policy=queue throughout 01:30-09:45) then FAST from 10:00 (applied at 10:00:29, total_slots=3 by 10:05).
- The report classified 153/153 sessions (100%) as Fast and 0 as Cheap, and showed 'slots: 3' for all sessions, because the analysis ran at 11:47 in fast mode and config-fast.yaml has a single 3-slot bucket (23:59->3, 10:00->3 -> equal counts collapse to one 'fast' bucket).

## Impact

- Fast/cheap split columns in report.md, fast_sessions.csv, cheap_sessions.csv are wrong for any window crossing 01:00/10:00 transitions (or a manual API mode switch).
- 'slots' column and per-slot context figures are wrong (report used 43691 = 131072/3; overnight the real per-slot context was 131072 = 262144/2 under cheap).
- Recommendations citing fast/cheap splits inherit the error.

## Evidence

Mode transitions are logged and parseable:
  'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode cheap' / '... fast'
  'Mode scheduler: enabled with 2 entries: ...'
Status lines expose the active profile: total_slots=<n> and contention_queue_policy=queue|fallback.

## Proposed fix (ACs)

1. The script parses 'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode <mode>' lines from proxy.log* to build a per-timestamp mode timeline covering the window.
2. Each session's fast/cheap bucket is keyed by the mode active at its first in-window stream time (falling back to current-mode config when no transition is observed in the window, e.g. single-mode windows).
3. Cheap sessions appear in cheap_sessions.csv; the report's Total/Fast/Cheap columns reflect the actual mode split (verified against a window spanning 01:00-11:00: ~9h cheap + 1h fast, not 100% fast).
4. 'slots' and per-slot context in CSV/report reflect the profile active for that session (2/262144 for cheap, 3/131072 for fast).
5. Existing tests pass; add a regression fixture using real 'Mode scheduler' + status_request lines.

## Notes

- Window-only reconstruction: sessions starting before the earliest observed transition in the window use the profile implied by the nearest prior transition in available logs (or analysis-time mode as today).
- Keep the existing behavior for windows entirely inside one mode (no transition observed): bucketing from the analysis-time config is correct there.
data.title: Proxy usage analysis: fast/cheap bucketing uses analysis-time config, not the mode active during the window

# Bug: proxy-usage-analysis hourly table hides real activity — session-first-hour attribution, no per-hour traffic columns, and duplicate hour-of-day buckets yield impossible >100% rows

## Problem statement

The `## Summary by hour` table in the proxy-usage-analysis report
(`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) misrepresents hourly activity in three
compounding ways: it counts sessions only in the hour of their **first**
request (so long-running sessions contribute nothing to later hours), it has
no columns for the traffic actually attributable to each hour, and its
window-bounded rows are keyed by **hour-of-day** so a rolling 24h window
emits two rows that share one busy-duration bucket — producing impossible
busy percentages (observed `327.5%` in archived `2026-09-12_5` and
`118250.9%` in the latest `report.md`).

## Users

- **Operator / proxy maintainer** reading the daily report to decide whether
  the local models are being used well and why traffic fell back.

Example user stories:

- As the proxy maintainer, I want each hour's row to show how much traffic
  actually occurred in that hour, so that busy hours do not look empty just
  because their sessions started earlier.
- As the proxy maintainer, I want the hourly busy percentage to be a
  trustworthy number (never above 100%), so that I can trust the report when
  tuning slot counts and routing thresholds.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `## Summary by hour` table includes per-hour **activity columns
   counted by event timestamp** within each bucket (not by session start
   hour): `Requests started` (all `Stream started` events), `Local attempts`
   (`Stream started` with `provider=local`), `Local served` (`Stream finished`
   with `provider=local`), `Fallbacks` (`Fallback triggered` events), and
   `Local-skip` (`routing_skip_local` events). The misleading
   session-first-hour classification columns are replaced by these activity
   columns.
2. Hour buckets are keyed by **absolute wall-clock hour** (not hour-of-day),
   so a rolling window emits exactly one row per distinct hour bucket; no
   row's busy duration duplicates another row's, and no row shows a busy
   percentage greater than 100% (busy% is busy / window-bounded bucket
   duration and is defensively clamped to 100%).
3. A deterministic regression test reproduces the rolling-window case (24h
   window starting at `HH:04`, e.g. `2026-09-11 11:04 → 2026-09-12 11:04`)
   with synthetic events spread across the afternoon, and asserts that: (a)
   the `12:00–18:00` rows are non-zero and their `Requests started` total
   matches the fixture, and (b) no row's busy% exceeds 100% and no two rows
   report the same busy duration; new tests cover both the duplicate-bucket
   case and the per-hour attribution, and the existing suite in
   `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` continues to pass.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments and the proxy-usage-analysis `SKILL.md` (the table's column
   semantics and hour-bucket keying).
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. Implemented via the standard worktree workflow (implement skill), not the
   main checkout.

## Constraints

- Only the project-local skill at `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` is in
  scope (scripts, tests, `SKILL.md`); this is the explicit target of the
  work item.
- The report is generated from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`; parsing
  and window semantics (`window_start <= ts <= window_end`) must not change.
- Report output is operator-facing Markdown plus a `--json` summary; the JSON
  export (`hourly_busy`, `hourly_session_classification`) is adjusted to
  match the new keying but should stay machine-readable and self-describing.
- The historical `proxy.log` for `2026-09-11/12` has been rotated away
  (only `llama-server` logs for those dates remain), so AC3's historical
  window is validated with a synthetic fixture rather than the original logs.

## Existing state

- `reporting.py::_append_summary_by_hour` iterates window-bounded buckets from
  `window_start`, truncating the first/last rows to the window edges, and
  looks up busy seconds via `summary.busy.hourly_busy` keyed by hour-of-day.
- `reporting.py::_hourly_session_classification` counts each session once,
  in the hour of its first `Stream started` event.
- `aggregation.py::_attribute_interval` accumulates busy seconds into
  `hourly[mid.hour]` (hour-of-day key).
- `aggregation.py::BusyStats.hourly_busy` is `list[tuple[int, float]]`
  (hour-of-day → seconds).
- Known artifacts in produced reports:
  - latest `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`, window
    `2026-09-24 05:00:01 → 2026-09-25 05:00:01`:
    `| 05:00-05:00 | 26m 52s | 118250.9% |` (duplicate hour-of-day row).
  - archived `2026-09-12_5`:
    `| 10:00-10:12 | 41m 54s | 327.5% |` alongside
    `| 10:12-11:00 | 41m 54s | 88.7% |` (same busy duration, two rows).

## Desired change

1. **Per-hour attribution.** Add per-hour activity counters derived from the
   in-window event lists (`summary.sessions`, `summary.fallback_events`,
   `summary.routing_skip_events`) keyed by each event's timestamp bucket, and
   render them as new table columns. Recompute the Totals row as the sum of
   each activity column over the window.
2. **Absolute-hour keying.** Change busy attribution to key by the absolute
   hour (`mid.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)`), update
   `BusyStats.hourly_busy` accordingly (absolute hour → seconds), and look up
   per-row busy by the row's absolute hour. Defensively clamp busy% to 100%.
3. **Tests.** Update the existing `Summary by hour` tests for the new columns
   and keying; add the rolling-window regression test described in AC3.
4. **Docs.** Update the `_append_summary_by_hour` and
   `_hourly_session_classification` docstrings, the `hourly_busy` JSON
   docstring, and `SKILL.md` to describe the columns and absolute-hour
   keying.

**Key Files:**

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Rework
  `_append_summary_by_hour` (columns, absolute-hour lookup, clamp, totals) and
  replace `_hourly_session_classification` with per-hour activity counters;
  update `_hourly_session_classification_json` / the JSON export.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Key
  `_attribute_interval` / `BusyStats.hourly_busy` by absolute hour and update
  the `BusyStats` docstring.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` —
  Update the hourly-table tests and add the rolling-window duplicate-bucket
  and per-hour activity attribution tests.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — Document the new columns and
  absolute-hour bucketing.

**Related work:**

- **LP-0MTFO210Q0044TTF** – proxy-usage-analysis: add per-hour request-start
  classification columns to hourly table (completed) — introduced the
  session-first-hour columns and the hour-of-day keying looked up here.
- **LP-0MSVMLM7G009N74N** – Proxy usage report: retitle hourly busy table to
  'Busy time by hour', bound hours to report window, add % column and totals
  row (completed) — introduced the window-bounded partial rows that expose
  the duplicate-bucket defect.
- **LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT** – proxy-usage-analysis: report server-side
  compactions and fallback avoidance impact (completed).
- **LP-0MTTPXIAB0031AC4** – Add retry logic to proxy summarizer on transient
  failures (R3) (completed).
- **LP-0MRI8JFV4006C43X** – Config and dispatch N-awareness implementation
  (completed).

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items

- **LP-0MTTPXIAB0031AC4** – Add retry logic to proxy summarizer on transient failures (R3) (completed)
- **LP-0MRI8JFV4006C43X** – Config and dispatch N-awareness implementation (completed)
- **LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT** – proxy-usage-analysis: report server-side compactions and fallback avoidance impact (completed)

#### Repository file matches

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 10s, acceptance, activity, actually, analysis (+120 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: 10s, acceptance, activity, actually, analysis (+120 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: 10s, acceptance, activity, actually, analysis (+120 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1 — replace, not append, the session-start columns.** The
  three session-first-hour classification columns are replaced by the
  per-hour activity columns; per-session journey classification remains
  available in the `## Session summary` section. Retaining both would widen
  the table and keep the misleading signal. (If the producer prefers to keep
  the start-journey columns as extra columns, this is a additive change.)
- **Assumption A2 — definition of the activity columns.** `Local served`
  counts local `Stream finished` events (streams completed on the local
  provider), not distinct sessions; `Fallbacks` counts `Fallback triggered`
  events; `Local-skip` counts `routing_skip_local` events. A local attempt
  that later falls back therefore appears in both `Local attempts` and
  `Fallbacks` (different events).
- **Assumption A3 — "no two rows for the same hour-of-day" (AC2).** For a
  24h window that straddles an hour (e.g. `11:04 → 11:04`), hour-of-day 11
  legitimately appears at both window edges. The defect being fixed is
  *duplicate bucket keys / duplicated busy duration*, not the existence of
  two edge partials. AC2 is therefore met by absolute-hour keying plus the
  clamp, not by suppressing one edge row.
- **Risk — JSON schema change.** `BusyStats.hourly_busy` changes from
  hour-of-day integers to absolute-hour keys and
  `hourly_session_classification` is reshaped. No in-repo consumer other than
  `reporting.py` and the tests was found, but the `--json` output is
  machine-readable and the change should be documented.
- **Risk — historical logs unavailable.** AC3 cannot be validated against the
  original `2026-09-11/12` proxy log (rotated away); the fixture-based
  regression is the accepted substitute.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Additional opportunities (e.g. per-hour columns in
  the CSVs, a wider column set, or hourly error breakdowns) are out of scope
  and should be captured as separate linked work items rather than folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The work item already contained an
RCA-derived problem statement, three (expanded to six) acceptance criteria,
the observed artefacts, and the two related predecessor work items, which was
sufficient to draft this brief. The interpretation choices above (A1–A3) are
recorded as documented assumptions rather than unanswered questions, and the
draft is presented for producer feedback without blocking.

- Q: (none asked) — n/a. Source: n/a.
data.title: proxy-usage-analysis: hourly table hides real activity (session-first-hour attribution, no per-hour traffic columns, duplicate hour-of-day buckets give >100% rows)

# Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion — accurate diagnostics, quarantine visibility, bounded chain-hold

## Context

Overnight (local 02:00–05:00 and 07:00–11:00 = **UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00**), remote-only
fallback chains exhaust. Every remote tier in the `plan`/`author`/`code` chains is gated by
`available_times`, and the only always-on provider (`local-qwen3`) is refused by the router for
oversized/uncompactable sessions (`_route_remote_with_compaction_guidance`,
`proxy/proxy/router.py:676`). The proxy then returns a 503 whose text is:

    All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window

That message is wrong (the dominant blockers were usage-limit quarantine and a failed compaction
summarizer) and is not matched by the client recovery classifier, producing `Unrecognized error:`.

## Evidence (2026-09-16/17)

- Config: `proxy/config.yaml:256` and siblings — `available_times: ["00:00-01:00","04:00-06:00","10:00-00:00"]`
  leaves UTC gaps 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00.
- `proxy.log.2026-09-16_01` @ 02:20 local:
  `compaction_remote_with_guidance ... refusing local near-full-slot dispatch` →
  `Skipping opencode-go-3/-2: usage_limit_reset_pending` →
  `Skipping opencode-go/deepseek-flash: outside its available_times window` →
  `All providers exhausted ... unavailable={}` → `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s (cycle=0, max_cycles=3)`.
- Exhaustion events by hour cluster exactly in the two UTC gaps; ~0 outside them.

## Children

1. Time-window-specific 503 only when **every** provider was window-skipped.
2. Expose usage-limit quarantine in exhaustion diagnostics and in `retry_after`.
3. Bound chain-hold by the real `retry_after`.
4. Stable machine-readable exhaustion error code (client classification).

## Related

- LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC (timed access feature), LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 (honest Retry-After),
  LP-0MU1RXEPL005CK97 (remote tier stalls), and the compaction RCA created alongside this epic.

# render_report.py reads auditResult but wl show exposes audit under 'audit' (report always shows 'Audit: not run')

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report renderer never shows the real audit verdict: `render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")`, but `wl show <id> --json` places the structured verdict at the **top level** of the payload (`auditResult.readyToClose`, a boolean), mirroring it into `workItem.audit` (an object with `time`/`author`/`text`/`status` for backwards compatibility) — it is never present as a boolean inside `workItem`. Because `render_from_wl()` passes only `data["workItem"]` to the renderer, the field is always missing and every report renders `- **Audit:** ❔ not run`, even when the work item carries a passing canonical audit.

**Confirmed empirically** on LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB: the top-level `auditResult` is `{..., "readyToClose": true, ...}` and `workItem.audit.status` is `"Complete"`, yet `render_report.py LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` prints `- **Audit:** ❔ not run`.

## Users

- **Skill agents** (intake, plan, implement, audit, ship) that render the report as their final step and paste it verbatim.
- **Producers/operators** who read reports to decide whether an audit has passed and whether to advance or release a work item.
- **Automation authors** whose scripts and tests consume the rendered report or the documented `auditResult` payload shape.

Example user stories:

- As an **audit/implement agent**, I want the report's Audit line to reflect the persisted verdict, so my final report is not self-contradictory.
- As a **producer**, I want `✅ passed` shown when `auditResult.readyToClose` is true, so I do not waste effort re-running or second-guessing an audit that already passed.
- As an **automation author**, I want the renderer to read the payload shape documented in `skill/report/SKILL.md`, so I can test the report against real `wl show --json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Structured verdict is respected.** Given a `wl show <id> --json` payload whose top-level `auditResult` is `{"readyToClose": true}` (or `false`), the rendered Meta-Data line is `- **Audit:** ✅ passed` (or `❌ failed`). Verified by unit tests over realistic payloads.
2. **Correct wiring on both entry points.** `render_from_wl()` threads the envelope's top-level `auditResult` into the metadata, and the `--json` stdin path handles the full `{workItem, auditResult}` envelope without dropping it. Verified by unit tests that feed a canned envelope (no live `wl`).
3. **Absent / legacy fallbacks.** A null or missing `auditResult` renders `❔ not run`; a legacy boolean `workItem.auditResult` and a legacy `workItem.audit` object (`status: "Complete"`, or text whose first line starts with `Ready to close: Yes`/`No`) still resolve to the correct verdict. Verified by unit tests covering each fallback.
4. **Regression coverage.** A regression test captures the observed failure shape (top-level `auditResult.readyToClose: true`, `workItem.auditResult` absent) and asserts `passed`; re-rendering a real audited item (LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB) shows `✅ passed` instead of `not run`.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/report/SKILL.md` (the Meta-Data source table and Audit row), and any relevant docs-site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix lives in the canonical SorraAgents source `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`; `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/` is a symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/report/` — do not edit through the symlink ad hoc.
- Preserve the public library API: `render_metadata()` / `render_report_from_workitem()` must keep working for callers that pass only a `workItem` dict. New parameters must be optional.
- `auditResult.readyToClose` (top-level, structured) is the authoritative source; `workItem.audit` is a backwards-compatibility mirror only. Do not make `workItem.audit` the primary source.
- Do not depend on live `wl` in unit tests — inject fixtures / patch the subprocess, matching the existing test style.
- Reuse the existing `AUDIT_ICONS` mapping (`yes`/`no`/`unknown`); do not invent new icons.
- Keep the canonical report template contract unchanged: the Meta-Data field name and `- **Audit:**` line stay as-is (only the derived value changes).
- No behavioural drift for already-correct fields (Type/Priority/Status/Stage/Risk/Effort/Children).

## Existing state

- `render_metadata()` (line ~235) reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` and expects a boolean (`True` → passed, `False` → failed). The real payload never has that key inside `workItem`, so it always yields `unknown` → `not run`.
- `render_from_wl()` fetches `wl show <id> --json --children`, then uses only `data.get("workItem", {})` and `data.get("children", [])`; the envelope-level `data["auditResult"]` is discarded.
- The `--json` stdin branch does `work_item = data.get("workItem", data)`, likewise discarding an envelope-level `auditResult`.
- `wl show --json` (ContextHub `dist/commands/show.js` lines ~79–92) sets `result.auditResult = db.getAuditResult(item.id)` and, when present, mirrors it into `result.workItem.audit = {time, author, text, status}`. So the audit is a sibling of `workItem`, not a field on it.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` already documents the correct source: `Audit | auditResult (null → not run; readyToClose true/false)`. The code simply does not implement the documented contract.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` fabricates `"auditResult": true` *inside* the work-item fixture, a shape that never occurs in practice, so no test detected the defect.
- The failed-audit case is symmetric: `auditResult.readyToClose: false` also renders `not run` today, masking `❌ failed`.

## Desired change

Thread the structured verdict from the `wl show` envelope into metadata derivation and normalise the verdict from all known payload shapes.

1. `render_metadata(work_item, children=None, audit_result=None)` — accept an optional structured `audit_result`. Derive `yes`/`no`/`unknown` with precedence:
   1. `audit_result["readyToClose"]` when `audit_result` is a mapping and the key is present (authoritative);
   2. legacy boolean `work_item.get("auditResult")` (keeps callers using simple dicts working);
   3. legacy `work_item.get("audit")` mapping → `status == "Complete"` and/or first line of `text` starting `Ready to close: Yes` / `No`;
   4. otherwise `unknown` → `❔ not run`.
2. `render_report_from_workitem(..., audit_result=None)` — pass `audit_result` through to `render_metadata`.
3. `render_from_wl()` — pass `data.get("auditResult")` into `render_report_from_workitem`.
4. `main()` `--json` stdin path — when the piped payload is the full envelope, pass `data.get("auditResult")` alongside `data["workItem"]`.
5. Tests — replace the unrealistic fixture shape with realistic envelope(s); add cases for `readyToClose` true/false, absent/null, legacy boolean, legacy `audit` object, and the observed regression payload.
6. Docs/comments — update `skill/report/SKILL.md` and the code docstring/comments to state the exact source and fallback precedence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — `render_metadata()` (audit derivation), `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()`, `main()` `--json` branch. Adds optional `audit_result` plumbing and a small verdict-normalisation helper.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — realistic `wl show --json` envelope fixtures; new audit-metadata unit tests (structured true/false, absent, legacy boolean, legacy object, regression case).
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Meta-Data source-of-truth table (Audit row) and any notes describing the verdict source; confirm it matches the implemented precedence.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/dist/commands/show.js` — read-only reference for the payload shape (`auditResult` top-level, `workItem.audit` mirror); no change expected.

## Related work

- **LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB** — Server-side compaction is unreachable for oversized sessions (the `discovered-from:LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` item; its passing audit was misreported as `not run`).
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill (umbrella; open, `plan_complete`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Choosing the wrong source of truth (text parsing vs structured boolean) could reintroduce ambiguity for manual approvals, whose `summary` is free text (e.g. "Approved by manual review") and may not contain a `Ready to close:` line. **Mitigation:** prefer structured `auditResult.readyToClose`; only fall back to text/`status` for legacy payloads, and cover each path with a test.
- **Risk:** Changing the public signature of `render_metadata`/`render_report_from_workitem` could break external callers. **Mitigation:** new parameters are optional and keyword-defaulted; existing positional calls keep working.
- **Risk:** Tests could keep passing while the CLI path remains broken (the current blind spot). **Mitigation:** add a test that exercises `render_from_wl()` end-to-end against a stubbed `wl show` envelope, not just `render_report_from_workitem()`.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into the audit subsystem (persist/verdict logic). **Mitigation:** this item is read-path only — no changes to `skill/audit/**` or to how verdicts are persisted.

- **Assumption:** `Audit: not run` must remain the rendering for a genuinely unaudited item (`auditResult` null/absent) — the fix must not fabricate a verdict.
- **Scope creep:** Does not address audit freshness/staleness rendering, TUI audit icons, or the `Audit Read Path` read-cost work; those remain separate items.

No operator questions were required — the seed description plus repository inspection were sufficient to draft this brief. The following research-derived answers close what would otherwise have been interview questions (all self-answered; evidence is a file path, command, or work-item id).

- **Q: Where does `wl show --json` actually expose the audit verdict?**

Evidence: `ContextHub` `dist/commands/show.js` lines ~79–92; `wl show LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB --json`.
- **Q: Is `workItem.auditResult` ever populated?**
  - Answer: No — it is always absent/null for the current `wl` version, which is why the renderer always says `not run`. Evidence: `wl show LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB --json` ⇒ `workItem.auditResult: None`, top-level `auditResult.readyToClose: True`.
- **Q: Which source should the fix prefer?**
  - Answer: The structured top-level `auditResult.readyToClose`, matching `skill/report/SKILL.md`'s documented contract; text parsing of `workItem.audit` is only a legacy fallback. Evidence: `skill/report/SKILL.md` line ~107.
- **Q: Which repository/path is the canonical source to edit?**
  - Answer: `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`; the `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/` path in the bug description is a symlink to it. Evidence: `ls -la /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills` ⇒ symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`.
- **Q: Do the existing tests cover this path?**
  - Answer: No — they use a fabricated `workItem.auditResult` boolean and never exercise `render_from_wl`'s envelope extraction. Evidence: `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` lines ~35, ~50.
- **Q: Was the defect reproduced before filing?**
  - Answer: Yes: `python3 .../render_report.py LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` printed `- **Audit:** ❔ not run` for an item with a passing persisted audit. Source: this intake session, command output.
